unit-help: A street's color is its full score: the problems and features along the block, averaged with the crossings at its ends. A neighborhood is the length-weighted mean of its audited streets.
weights-help: A weight multiplies a factor's effect. The bar under each slider is that factor's average effect per street.
updated-never: Scores appear after the first nightly clustering run.
tip-standout-feature-better: Stands out: {{type}} helps more here ({{value}} per street vs {{city}} citywide)
tip-standout-feature-worse: Stands out: {{type}} helps less here ({{value}} per street vs {{city}} citywide)
tip-standout-problem-better: Stands out: {{type}} costs less here ({{value}} per street vs {{city}} citywide)
tip-standout-problem-worse: Stands out: {{type}} costs more here ({{value}} per street vs {{city}} citywide)
show-clusters-help: Access Score is built on these sidewalk label clusters. Clusters appear once you zoom in to street level. You can click on clusters to see their underlying imagery.
dark-map-help: A dark basemap with a ramp stepped for it, so the scores carry the picture.
updated-help: The scores are recomputed from the label clusters on a schedule; labels added since then are folded in at the next run.
cluster-open: Click to open it in the imagery
zoom-in-for-clusters: Zoom in to see the clusters
chart-histogram-help: How much sidewalk sits at each score. Drag across the bars to pick a range; the map dims everything outside it.
chart-rank-help: Every neighborhood with enough data, best first. Click one to go there.
rank-empty: No neighborhood has enough data yet.
chart-whats-here-help: The clusters behind the scores in view, by label type and rating — on the streets and at the crossings of the selected neighborhood or street, or the whole city, narrowed by a picked range.
whats-here-empty: No scored streets in this range.
chart-photos-help: Pictures of the labels behind the scores, from the selected neighborhood or street, or from the lowest-scoring neighborhood when nothing is selected. Ranked worst first: the worst-rated labels lead, and among those, the ones the community has confirmed. Click one to open it.
places-help: Schools, health care, libraries, grocery stores, transit stops, parks, and community centers, from OpenStreetMap, so a score can be read against where people need to go. Schools, health care, and libraries show at city scale; the rest once you zoom in to street level. Click a place for the score of the street it sits on.
places-unavailable: Places aren't available for this city yet.
show-grade-help: Colors every street by how steep it is instead of by its AccessScore. Slope comes from an elevation model, not from labels, so unaudited streets have it too. While this is on, every street with a slope is drawn, so “Show unaudited streets” has no effect.
slope-quality-structure: This street is on a bridge or in a tunnel, which the elevation model cannot see, so it has no slope.
slope-quality-suspect: The elevation model looked unreliable here, so this slope is a straight line between the street's two ends.
slope-quality-no-data: The elevation model has no data under this street.
slope-approximate: From a coarse elevation model, so treat these numbers as approximate.
profile-label: Elevation profile along the street: {{start}} at the start, {{end}} at the end, lowest {{low}}, highest {{high}}.
profile-failed: The elevation profile could not be loaded.
profile-none: No elevation profile is available for this street.
